hyperedges.label: Multi-Agent Coordination (Commander orchestrates specialized agents via knowledge layer)

nodes.label: Autonomous Agent System — Multi-Agent Architecture
nodes.rationale: AQRTI uses specialized narrow-responsibility agents instead of one monolithic AI so each agent can be independently improved, replaced, or scaled. Agent communication via message queues and a knowledge layer decouples producers from consumers.

nodes.label: Backtesting Framework
nodes.rationale: Backtests alone can lie (curve-fitting); therefore walk-forward validation and Monte Carlo simulation are required in addition to historical backtesting to ensure a strategy actually has edge, not just overfit parameters.

nodes.label: Data Architecture — Foundation Layer
nodes.rationale: Data quality takes priority over model complexity because all downstream outputs (predictions, strategies, learning) degrade with bad data. Raw data is immutable and stored forever because the historical intelligence repository cannot be replaced — it is the primary competitive moat.

nodes.label: Execution Engine — Signal Delivery & Trade Execution
nodes.norm_label: execution engine — signal delivery & trade execution

nodes.label: Execution Phases (Research→Paper→Semi-Auto→Autonomous)
nodes.rationale: Execution is gated in four phases — research only, then paper trading, then human-approved semi-automation, then fully autonomous — to prevent premature deployment of capital before the system earns trust.

nodes.label: Learning Engine — Self-Improvement & Knowledge Evolution
nodes.rationale: Mistakes and failures are stored permanently and converted into training assets so the system compounds intelligence over market cycles instead of repeating errors.

nodes.label: Confidence Calibration
nodes.rationale: 83% predicted confidence should yield 83% real accuracy. Calibration drift is monitored to prevent overconfidence, which is one of the primary failure categories.

nodes.label: Learning Database (knowledge_predictions, knowledge_strategies, knowledge_regimes, knowledge_failures, knowledge_patterns)
nodes.norm_label: learning database (knowledge_predictions, knowledge_strategies, knowledge_regimes, knowledge_failures, knowledge_patterns)

nodes.label: Model Architecture — Ensemble Intelligence Core
nodes.rationale: Single models fail; AQRTI uses an ensemble where every prediction is a consensus. A meta-intelligence layer dynamically re-weights models based on recent performance to prevent any single model from dominating incorrectly.

nodes.label: Model E — Market Regime Model
nodes.rationale: No strategy is executed before regime classification because the same strategy that works in a bull market can destroy capital in a panic market. Regime detection gates all downstream decisions.

nodes.label: Model Promotion Pipeline (Dev→Test→Validation→Shadow→Paper→Production)
nodes.rationale: No model may skip stages to prevent premature deployment of untested models that could cause capital loss.

nodes.label: Model Training Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Never train on future data and never leak information — every model must earn deployment through walk-forward and paper validation before production use.

nodes.label: Paper Trading Engine — Virtual Capital Validation
nodes.rationale: Paper trading is the bridge between backtesting and live deployment because backtests can lie but markets do not. Minimum 60-day (recommended 120-day) period required before real capital is risked.
nodes.norm_label: paper trading engine — virtual capital validation

nodes.label: Pattern Matching Engine
nodes.rationale: Markets repeat patterns not exactly but closely enough to extract probabilities, making historical similarity search a useful intelligence multiplier for probability estimation.

nodes.label: Portfolio Optimization Engine
nodes.rationale: Finding opportunities is not enough — capital allocation determines actual performance. Higher confidence gets larger allocation; higher risk gets smaller allocation.

nodes.label: Risk Engine — Capital Preservation Framework
nodes.rationale: Survive first, profit second. A profitable system can recover from losses but a destroyed system cannot — therefore risk controls are non-negotiable gates before any execution.

nodes.label: Circuit Breakers (Auto-disable on abnormal loss/volatility/model failure)
nodes.norm_label: circuit breakers (auto-disable on abnormal loss/volatility/model failure)

nodes.label: Sentiment Engine — Market Psychology Measurement
nodes.rationale: Sentiment is measured to detect narrative changes before price fully reacts, giving early signals of momentum shifts.

nodes.label: Strategy Discovery Engine — Autonomous Alpha Generation
nodes.rationale: Static strategies eventually stop working as markets evolve. AQRTI treats every strategy as an experiment/hypothesis with a full lifecycle (generate→backtest→validate→paper trade→produce→retire) so the system is a strategy creator not just a strategy user.
nodes.norm_label: strategy discovery engine — autonomous alpha generation

nodes.label: Strategy Graveyard (Permanently stored failed strategies)
nodes.rationale: Failed strategies are never deleted so AQRTI can prevent repeating old mistakes — institutional knowledge of what failed, when, and why.
